Hwang-Shih-DeCani spending with an optimised parameter

Source: R/transform_pvalues_gsd_opt.R
sf_hsd_opt.Rd

sf_hsd_opt() tags a hypothesis whose Hwang-Shih-DeCani spending parameter should be chosen by graph_optimise_gsd() jointly with the graph, rather than fixed in advance. Pass it, alone or inside the list of spending functions, to transform_pvalues_gsd(), which then returns a multigrain_pvals_gsd_spec object instead of transformed p-values.

Usage

sf_hsd_opt(id = NULL, bounds = c(-4, 1), step = 0.25, start = NULL)

Arguments

id

NULL, or a single string or number naming the parameter. Hypotheses with the same id share one parameter, and the id is the name under which its value is reported.

bounds

A numeric vector of length 2: the lowest and highest value of the parameter to search. The lower bound must be at least -10, the upper at most 2, and the lower below the upper. Default is c(-4, 1).

step

The spacing of the lattice of values searched: one of 0.5, 0.25 or 0.125. Default is 0.25.

start

NULL or a number inside bounds: the value the search starts from, snapped to the nearest lattice node. NULL starts from the node nearest the midpoint of bounds.

Value

A spending function function(alpha, t, param) of class multigrain_sf_hsd_opt, returning gsDesign::sfHSD(alpha, t, param)$spend, with attributes id, bounds, step and start.

Details

The Hwang-Shih-DeCani parameter sets how quickly the level is spent: at an interim analysis at half the information, a parameter of -4 has spent about 12% of the level, a boundary like O'Brien and Fleming's, and a parameter of 1 about 62%, close to Pocock-type spending; 0 spends in proportion to information.

The parameter is searched over a lattice: the multiples of step inside bounds, together with both bounds (21 nodes for the defaults). Every node's boundary table is built, and checked for well ordering and invertibility, when the spec is created, so every value the search can try is a valid group sequential transform. Building the tables takes about 0.9 s per node at the default grid_size of transform_pvalues_gsd() with two analyses; a progress bar is shown when it takes more than a couple of seconds.

Tagged hypotheses with the same id share one parameter. Tagged hypotheses without an id each get their own, except that a single sf_hsd_opt() passed as the whole spending argument (and so recycled across hypotheses) is one parameter shared by all of them. Hypotheses sharing a parameter must use identical bounds, step and start.

A tagged hypothesis with a single analysis at full information is not affected by its spending function and takes no part in the search; if that leaves no parameter to optimise, transform_pvalues_gsd() returns an ordinary multigrain_pvals_gsd object with a message.

See also

gsDesign::sfHSD(), transform_pvalues_gsd(), graph_optimise_gsd() for the search and the result, resolve_pvalues_gsd()

Examples

# one parameter shared by hypotheses 2 and 3, searched over -4, -3.5, ..., -2
spending <- list(
    gsDesign::sfLDOF,
    sf_hsd_opt(id = "secondary", bounds = c(-4, -2), step = 0.5),
    sf_hsd_opt(id = "secondary", bounds = c(-4, -2), step = 0.5)
)

set.seed(1)
raw <- array(stats::runif(100 * 3 * 2), dim = c(100L, 3L, 2L))
spec <- transform_pvalues_gsd(
    raw,
    info_frac = c(0.5, 1),
    spending = spending,
    grid_size = 64L
)
spec
#> <multigrain_pvals_gsd_spec>
#> 100 simulation(s), 3 hypothes(es), 2 analys(es); alpha = 0.025
#> Information fractions (NA = no data at that analysis):
#>    analysis 1 analysis 2
#> H1        0.5          1
#> H2        0.5          1
#> H3        0.5          1
#> Look-back: H1 = FALSE, H2 = FALSE, H3 = FALSE
#> Spending:
#> H1: spending[[1]]
#> H2: sfHSD(param = secondary in [-4, -2])
#> H3: sfHSD(param = secondary in [-4, -2])
#> Spending parameters:
#> secondary: bounds [-4, -2], step 0.5, 5 nodes, start -3
#> Boundary tables built: 5
